headline: Last session: Markets traded volatile amid global cues, crude oil movements, and foreign capital flows ahead of Diwali week.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 3 November.

why: FPIs pulled out ₹34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, though turning net buyers near the end of the month.
Crude oil prices remained elevated above $116, influencing overall market sentiment.
Strong festive demand drove domestic passenger vehicle dispatches past the five-lakh units mark in October.
Geopolitical risks and upcoming Q2 corporate earnings continue to steer broader market direction.
whatHappening: Stock markets saw volatile swings during recent sessions with India VIX rising amid global headwinds.
Eicher Motors registered a 7% increase in October total sales alongside a 47% jump in exports.
ONGC announced recruitment for 3,047 apprentice vacancies with applications open until November 20.
Investors are looking ahead to next week's trading session for signals on market rebound prior to Diwali.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets faced volatility driven by foreign fund flows and crude oil prices staying above $116. FPIs ended October as net buyers despite heavy outflows earlier in the month, while auto dispatches saw festive gains. Investors now focus on global cues, earnings, and geopolitical developments as the market prepares for the upcoming week.
